rows.my_view: Fair value; ~$67 sits on his $65 base at ~27-28x FY27 earnings with no margin of safety.
rows.committee: Agree it is fair, but the base case leans on FY2025's ZAR929M FCF, which the capex trend shows was the anomaly, not the normal year.

rows.my_view: High-teens, durable subscription growth of ~19% with record net additions.
rows.committee: Confirmed: ~19% four-year revenue CAGR and +22% in Q1, with the domestic engine genuinely intact.
FY2026 operating margin compressed 29%->26% with profit up only 8% on revenue up 20%, chipping the stable-margin assumption.

rows.my_view: Real switching-cost moat, but concentrated with ~76% of subscribers in South Africa.
rows.committee: Agree exactly: decade-durable switching-cost moat at home, but narrow and geographically trapped where the growth story needs it.

rows.my_view: Device investment is a deliberate land-grab; this is not capital-light SaaS.
rows.committee: Broadly agree, but capex grew ~34% CAGR while OCF grew ~17% and gross debt is 52% of market cap partly funding the build, so discipline is unproven.

rows.my_view: Valuation and South African currency/economic concentration.
rows.committee: The sharper risk is structural cash conversion at 3% of OCF, a business-quality question that a lower price alone would not fix.

rows.my_view: Framed the only thing holding him back as valuation.
rows.committee: The deeper blind spot is earnings-quality deterioration and the widening capex-vs-OCF scissors sitting beneath the price problem.

rows.my_view: Not specified beyond waiting on valuation.
rows.committee: The Oct 12 print: whether FCF recovers toward 20%+ of operating cash while subscriber growth holds settles the whole thesis.

confidence.label: Moderate
confidence.why: The posture and moat read hold up well, but the two thesis-defining questions (cash conversion, verified churn) are unresolved until the dated catalyst.

final_verdict: Correctly a watchlist: a genuinely good business at fair value where one October print will settle whether near-zero free cash flow is a phase or the natural state.
